Plots for Limma Result

autoplot.glystats_limma_res.Rd

Visualization for results from glystats::gly_limma() (glystats_limma_res objects). Only 2-group comparison is supported, and a volcano plot is drawn.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'glystats_limma_res'
autoplot(
  object,
  ...,
  contrast = NULL,
  log2fc_cutoff = 1,
  p_cutoff = 0.05,
  p_col = "p_adj",
  label = FALSE,
  point_size = 1.5,
  alpha = 0.7,
  title = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  fontsize = 9,
  family = "sans",
  palette = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A glystats_limma_res object.

...

Must be empty. Supply plotting controls by their full argument names.

contrast

A character string specifying the contrast to plot, in the format of "group1_vs_group2". Must be one of the contrasts in the result. When there is only one contrast (two-group comparison), it can be NULL (default).

log2fc_cutoff

The log2 fold change cutoff. Defaults to 1.

p_cutoff

The p-value cutoff. Defaults to 0.05.

p_col

The column name for p-value. Defaults to "p_adj". Can also be "p_val" (raw p-values without multiple testing correction).

label

Whether to label variables. Defaults to FALSE.

point_size, alpha

Point size and opacity.

title

Optional plot title. Defaults to NULL.

width, height

Plot-area dimensions in millimetres. NULL uses the tidyplots defaults (50 by 50 mm); NA fills the available graphics device. These are not export-page dimensions.

fontsize

Base text size in points. Defaults to 9.

family

Font family. Defaults to "sans".

palette

Color vector. A named vector maps group names to fixed colors across plots and subsets; unnamed palettes follow factor order. NULL selects the plot-specific default: blue-white-red for continuous heatmaps, directional colors for volcano and S-plots, selection colors for ranked dot plots, and distinct hues for other plots.

Value

A tidyplot object, also inheriting from ggplot.

Fold-change availability

A volcano plot requires at least one non-missing log2fc value in the selected comparison. Results with only missing fold changes produce an informative error rather than an empty plot. This includes logx results and unlogged raw-scale limma analyses, whose native estimates are not log2 fold changes. Native estimates are never substituted for log2fc. When only some fold changes are missing, the available values are plotted without changing the supplied results.

See also

glyvis_plot_options for common styling options.
